title: Bidirectional BFS in Porto Alegre: Meet in the Middle!
description: Watch Bidirectional BFS race from start and goal at the same time, shrinking the search space dramatically. The visualization simulates navigating a real street-like graph through Tristeza’s grid-style connectivity.
ig_caption:
🚦🌍 **Bidirectional BFS** is the speedrun of unweighted pathfinding: we start BFS from **both** the source and the destination, expanding the frontier layer-by-layer until they **meet in the middle**. 🧠

📌 **Graph theory angle:** Treat the street map as an **unweighted graph** where intersections are nodes and roads are edges. Bidirectional BFS finds the shortest path (in edge count) by guaranteeing the earliest meeting of the two BFS waves, typically reducing explored nodes from ~b^d to about ~2·b^(d/2) for branching factor *b* and path length *d*. ⚡

🗺️ In this reel, the algorithm “fans out” from both ends, then reconstructs the route using the two search trees—like plotting a back-and-forth route through Porto Alegre (Tristeza). ✅

🎥 Want me to visualize the same city with A* or Dijkstra next? Comment **“NEXT”** and hit follow for more real-map algorithm builds! 🤝
fb_caption:
🚶‍♂️💡 In unweighted graphs, **Bidirectional BFS** is a smart twist on classic BFS: it searches forward from the start and backward from the goal simultaneously. When the two frontiers meet, you instantly get the shortest path in number of edges—perfect for street-map style connectivity.

📍In this Porto Alegre (Tristeza) visualization, think of intersections as nodes and roads as edges, and watch how expanding from both ends dramatically reduces the search area.
